**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Support filter_by() from columns, functions, Core SQL** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2798

issue.title: filter_by() doesn't derive the entity from func calls, maybe other expressions

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Using a callable with context as a default value breaks badly when triggering a query within it.

**Expected behavior**
No error, and correctly querying the default value, like it was the case before 1.4

**To Reproduce**

```py
from sqlalchemy import *
from sqlalchemy.orm import *


Base = declarative_base()



def _get_next_position(context):
    parent_id = context.current_parameters['parent_id']
    res = s.query(func.max(Category.position)).filter_by(parent_id=parent_id).one()
    return (res[0] or 0) + 1


class Category(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'categories'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('categories.id'), index=True, nullable=True)
    position = Column(SmallInteger, nullable=False, default=_get_next_position)
    children = relationship('Category', primaryjoin=(id == remote(parent_id)),
                            backref=backref('parent', primaryjoin=(remote(id) == parent_id)))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Category {self.id} @{self.position}>'


e = create_engine('postgresql:///test', echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)
s = Session(e)


root = Category()
Category(parent=root)
Category(parent=root)
s.add(root)
s.commit()

print(s.query(Category).all())

```
